{{nihongo|'''Nishiteru Shrine'''|西照神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Awa Province (Tokushima)]].

'''Nishiteru Shrine'''（にしてるじんじゃ）is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Wakimachi|Q28689983|qid=Q28689983|lt=Wakimachi}}, {{ill|Mima, Tokushima|Q857828|qid=Q857828}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|Q160734|qid=Q160734}}, and is also called "Tsukigami-no-miya" (Shrine of the Moon Deity). It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=shikinai small shrine}}. Under the former {{ill|Q712534|lt=shrine ranking system}}, it was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. The main deity is Tsukuyomi Ōkami ({{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|qid=Q595520|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}}), with the three Munakata goddesses as associated deities: {{ill|Tagitsuhime|Q10932592|qid=Q10932592|lt=Tagitsuhime-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Tagorihime|Q10932870|qid=Q10932870|lt=Tagorihime-no-Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|Q11059454|qid=Q11059454|qid=Q11059454|lt=Ichikishimahime-no-Mikoto}}.

It is treated as a candidate shrine for Tajiki Shrine listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}.

According to shrine tradition, Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, ruler of the land of night, dispatched Tajikitsuhime-no-Mikoto to Ōtaki-yama as an inspector toward {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}}, and from here had her watch over the {{ill|Seto Inland Sea|Q231312|qid=Q231312}}; this is said to be the shrine's origin.

It is said that in the early {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, {{ill|Kūkai|Q222227|qid=Q222227}} practiced ascetic training on this mountain and installed Nishiteru Daigongen, making it a mountain training site of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shinbutsu-shūgō}}.

Until the {{ill|Meiji era|lt=Meiji period|qid=Q3125096}}, it was called "Nishiteru Gongen." In the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}, it was venerated by the Inada clan, {{ill|Karō|Q1316445|qid=Q1316445}} of the {{ill|Tokushima Domain|Q3034557|qid=Q3034557}}, who donated 9 chō 8 tan of shrine land, and by the lords of the {{ill|Takamatsu Domain|Q1036915|qid=Q1036915}}, who donated 50 koku for operating expenses as their prayer site.

In the early Meiji era, the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shinbutsu bunri edict}} separated the shrine from its temple ({{ill|Otaki-ji Temple|Q11437672|qid=Q11437672}}). * Legend of the komainu: The shrine has a {{ill|Komainu|Q20155846|qid=Q20155846}} dedicated in {{ill|Tenpō|Q1369045|qid=Q1369045}} 14 ({{ill|1843|Q7629|qid=Q7629}}). One summer night, a mother and child passing here were chased by a {{ill|Wolf|Q18498|qid=Q18498|lt=wolf}} and fled into the shrine. When the wolf tried to attack them, the komainu drove it away. Due to age, the old statue was moved to a safe place under the honden, and a new pair now stands at the former position by the stone steps.
===Precincts===
* First torii: Beside the road; stone steps continue from here into the precincts.
* Shrine office, kagura hall, and plaza
* Second torii
* Main shrine: haiden and honden
* Inari Shrine: deity is Uga-no-Mitama Ōkami. Haiden and honden are combined in one structure.
* Kumano Shrine: deities are Kumano Gongen, Izanagi Ōkami, and Izanami Ōkami. The Daigongen formerly enshrined at Okunoin of Mt. Ōtaki was moved here in early Shōwa.
* Hachidai Ryūō Shrine: deities are Nanda, Upananda, Sāgara, Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Anavatapta, Manasvin, and Utpalaka. Stone hokora.
* Prayer-stone area and votive horse painting "Tsuki no Mokuba" (painted by Fukuke Haruyo; completion ceremony 2019-11-10)
* Tōmei cedar: height 50 m, said to be 500 years old and known as a "thousand-year cedar." Tradition says the tip shone nightly at the start of the First Sino-Japanese War and went dark at peace talks; a similar event is also said for the Russo-Japanese War.
A parking lot is on the east pass side past Ōtaki-ji on Prefectural Route 106. A pair of komainu was installed at the east entrance in July 2025; walking about 50 m along the approach from there leads into the precincts.
The above shrine buildings line the crest running east from the summit one level above the shrine-office plaza.
